![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The pattern for handling CUDA version fallbacks is repeated in many places in this script. This code duplication makes the script harder to maintain and increases the risk of introducing bugs. For example, it's easy to have a mismatch between the logged fallback version and the one that is actually set.

To improve maintainability and make the script more robust, I recommend refactoring this logic into a helper function.

You could add a function like this near the top of the script:

```bash
_set_cuda_fallback() {
    local fallback_version=$1
    log "[INFO] Fallback: cuda_version=${cuda_version} -> cuda_version=${fallback_version}"
    cuda_version="${fallback_version}"
    cuda_version_without_dot="${cuda_version/./}"
}
```

Then, you can simplify this block and all similar ones by calling this function.

```suggestion
    if ! check_cuda_version 12.6 12.8 13.0; then
        _set_cuda_fallback "12.8"
    fi
```
